1142: Town of Pennington Gap RV park at the Leeman Field fairgrounds, beside the historic Leeman Field park (a seasonal pool, and a greenway with trout-stocked fishing access) and near the Stone Mountain ATV trailhead.  The RV pads sit in the open fairground lot, 150-250 m from the North Fork of the Powell River and out of sight of it; tent camping is along the river.  The fairgrounds hold ATV drag races, riding competitions, a rodeo and the Lee County Fair on some summer weekends. --Claude
1145: Wythe County campground on 90-acre Rural Retreat Lake, in the woods and set back from the water, which is reached by a trail or the boat launch; no RV site fronts or overlooks the lake.  There is a boat ramp, shoreline fishing (a Virginia license or access permit is needed from age 17), a trout pond, hiking trails, a playground and picnic shelters, and a swimming pool, closed for the 2026 season; swimming in the lake isn't allowed.  A site holds 6 people at most, alcohol isn't allowed, and quiet hours run from 11 p.m. to 7 a.m.  The campground's own phone is answered May to September; from October to April call 276-223-4517. --Claude
1198: Doddridge County Park's campground near West Union, an access point to the North Bend Rail Trail, with tent sites and three yurts beside its 24 RV slips.  Eight slips are asphalt and have sewer hookups; the other 16 are gravel, and their depths vary.  The park borders Meathouse Fork, but the creekside sites are the wooded tent sites, and the RV slips sit back from the creek.  The camp office has a store and a covered deck with a fireplace and television, Wi-Fi reaches the first ten slips, and the park has a pool from late May to early September, trails, playgrounds and courts. --Claude
1361: Family-owned campground on 60 acres around a 10-acre lake in Straughn, less than a mile off I-70, where every site is a 90-by-17-ft pull-through.  Most of the park is seasonal: 140 seasonal sites and 20 for short stays.  There is a swimming beach on the lake (no lifeguard), fishing, a basketball court, an ice-cream stand, a restaurant, a clubhouse and store and a playground, and fireworks light the lake on holiday weekends. --Claude
1372: Campground near Hartford City, formerly Wildwood Acres, with small fishing ponds that need no license, mini-golf and a meeting room; day visitors are welcome. --Claude
1473: Campground in the Finger Lakes wine country at Ovid, formerly Sned Acres, within walking distance of Cayuga Lake and 3 miles from the Dean's Cove boat launch.  It has shaded RV sites, cabins and rental RVs, a pool, three playgrounds, a fishing pond and a game room. --Claude
1498: Kittatinny Canoes' K-Camp on the Delaware River at Barryville, where the outfitter runs tubing, kayak, canoe and rafting trips; it also has cabins and rustic, creekside and riverfront tent sites.  RV sites are back-ins, some tucked along the creek; Campspot allows only pop-ups, tents, truck campers and vans onto the creekside ones. --Claude
1519: Happy Grounds campground at Blossvale, near Oneida Lake, with over 200 sites, most of them for long-term and seasonal guests, including a gated section for retirees.  Campspot sells it together with its sister park Riverbend East; in summer 48 Riverbend West sites are sold by the night, in three types.  There is a sandy beach, boat slips, an arcade, a playground, a country store, planned activities and on-site dining, and cabins and tent sites. --Claude
1990: Resort on a wooded bluff above a quiet no-wake cove of the Lake of the Ozarks at Sunrise Beach (mile marker 25), where most sites have concrete pads; boat and personal-watercraft slips are rented.  There is a saltwater pool, a hot tub, a fire pit, a playground, a fishing dock, a convenience store and laundry, golf carts to rent, tent sites, and long-term and seasonal sites. --Claude
2067: Resort and marina on Table Rock Lake at Kimberling City, where a hotel and cabins stand beside a campground in three areas: The Bluff, Middle Park and East Park.  Several site types look over the lake, and the full-hookup sites are in Middle Park.  Rates cover 4 people (age 4 and up), 6 at most, and there is a pool, a hot tub, a playground, sports courts, a fitness center and a dog park, plus boat slips at the marina. --Claude
2074: Campground east of Jefferson City, within walking distance of an Osage River access, whose water and electric back-in sites sit near a pond.  It has a playground, a covered pavilion, propane and firewood, and a clubhouse with games, a pool table, a large TV and air conditioning; pets and children are welcome.  Monthly stays are booked by phone, not online. --Claude
2078: Campground a mile from the Clearwater Lake dam near Piedmont, where every site has some shade and the water, electric and cable sites sit under tall pines.  There is a pool (no swimming in the Spring Branch), a playground, basketball, volleyball, horseshoes, an RC car track and fishing, and camper-style cabins and an RV are rented. --Claude
2593: RV park within walking distance of downtown Lake City's restaurants and shops, near the Alpine Loop Scenic Byway, with six rustic cabins and two cottages.  There is propane, ice, firewood, a bathhouse, laundry, a pavilion and a community fire pit.  A 2-night minimum has applied in peak season. --Claude
2625: Retro 1960s-themed resort in Cañon City, minutes from the Royal Gorge, that rents restored vintage trailers, cabins and apartments alongside its own RV and tent sites.  There is a seasonal heated pool, a hot tub, a year-round sauna, a dog park, a playground and lawn games, and karaoke and fire-truck hayrides in season. --Claude
3230: Family-owned RV park, built in 2020, half a mile from I-35 at Decatur City.  Its 17 pull-throughs are 80 ft long and its 9 back-ins 60 ft, with extra grass behind them, and tents may use any RV site.  There are private restrooms with showers, a playground and a common room to rent; pets are welcome, two at most. --Claude
3405: Large family campground at Lodi, near Madison and the Wisconsin Dells, where a swimming pond has water inflatables and a beach; there is also mini golf, a jumping pillow, giant shopping-cart rides, two playgrounds and themed weekends through the season, and seasonal sites.  Sites have water and electric, and a central dump station serves them; cabins, yurts, Conestoga wagons and park models are rented.  Rates cover 2 adults and 3 children (6 people at most), plus $10 for each extra person and $5 for each extra car; the renter must be 21 and stay on the site. --Claude
3903: Campground on M-123 near Newberry, about 20 minutes from Tahquamenon Falls, with fifty grassy pull-throughs, cabins and a cottage, and over a mile of nature trails through 40 acres of forest.  There is a playground, sand volleyball, an enclosed pavilion and a camp store, and snowmobile and ORV trails are nearby; the cabins also open for most of the snowmobile season.  A particular site is guaranteed only with the lock-site fee. --Claude
3926: Kinross Charter Township's RV park, 2.5 miles east of I-75 on M-80 (Tone Road), with 64 back-in sites on paved interior roads, some shaded.  There is a bathhouse with flush toilets and showers, a clubhouse for cards, board games and potlucks, horseshoes, picnic tables and fire pits; a campground host is there from mid-May to mid-September. --Claude
4320: City of Kings Mountain campground on John H. Moss Reservoir, with 22 wooded RV sites, all with full hookups and five of them pull-throughs, three tent sites, a heated bathhouse, a dump station and boat ramps.  Motorboats need a city permit; craft without a motor go free.  A stay may last two weeks, then campers must be away a week, and 70 days a year at most; alcohol isn't allowed, and quiet hours run from 10 p.m. to 6 a.m. --Claude
4449: Campground on TVA's Watts Bar Lake, family-owned since 2006 and a charter member of TVA's Camp-Right program, where every site is on or looks over the lake and has a fire pit with a grill and a picnic table.  Most sites have 50, 30 and 20 amps; 18 have only 30 and 20.  There are three bathhouses, a free dump station or a pump-out at the site ($30-45), a gated boat ramp, boat slips ($10 a night), two beaches, a camp store with live bait, laundry, propane, a playground, and kayaks, canoes, paddleboards and paddle boats to rent ($25-35 a day); Wi-Fi is at the office only.  Most of the campground closes in mid-November, but 25 sites stay open all year. --Claude
4753: Riverside resort on 65 acres by the Suwannee River at Mayo, with lodging from cabins to lodge rooms and two RV areas: Primrose Park for families (sites 101-236) and Key West Village for adults 21 and over (sites 300-469).  Its RV sites are 40 by 80 ft or larger, some of them fenced for pets, and there are heated pools and hot tubs (open all year), dog parks, laundry and a pet wash; Wi-Fi reaches some areas.  Lower Rendezvous, a separate area, has tent sites, water and electric sites for RVs to 20 ft and nine 30-amp full-hookup sites for RVs to 28 ft, without Wi-Fi or cable.  Long-term stays are in the Key West section. --Claude
4776: RV park just off I-10 at Lake City, under oaks, pines and magnolias, with pull-through sites, a heated saltwater pool, a stocked fishing pond, two fenced dog parks and a dog wash, a ninja obstacle course, a pavilion with a grill, a commercial kitchen and 24-hour laundry; cabins and park models are rented.  Pets may not be tied out, caged or fenced at the site. --Claude
5111: Locally owned RV park on US 29 at Wiggins, about 35 miles from the Mississippi beaches and 30 from Hattiesburg, with back-in and pull-through sites, fishing in its pond and Hobbs Creek, four private bathrooms with showers, coin laundry, a multipurpose room with fitness equipment, walking trails, horseshoes and croquet.  An efficiency cabin is rented. --Claude
5578: Country campground 2 miles east of downtown St. Cloud, with large open and wooded sites; staff lead each arrival to its site by golf cart.  It has a lodge with a snack bar, groceries and RV supplies, propane, a pool, a laundromat, firewood (outside firewood isn't allowed) and a 2,800-square-foot rally center with a kitchen.  For most of the season the guests are seniors, retirees and RV clubs, joined on summer weekends by families. --Claude
5677: City of Morris campground on Pomme de Terre Lake, with water and electric sites, tent sites, restrooms and showers, a spray park, a disc golf course, a dock, canoeing, fishing and a playground.  The city shuts the park's water off in mid-October; camping continues without it. --Claude
